trigger: Breach of security (unauthorized access of electronic data containing personal information: name with SSN, driver license or passport number, or geolocation) of Florida residents
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
notify: Each affected Florida individual by mail or email; notice must give the date or date range, the information involved, and a contact at the firm
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - most associates and candidates are Florida residents

obligation: Florida no-harm determination (alternative to individual notice)
trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement the firm reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept at least 5 years and provided to the Department of Legal Affairs within 30 days after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Only if counsel supports the determination; unlikely when SSNs were exported

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred; 15 more days if good cause is given in writing within the 30 days
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents (the associate register holds about 31,000 records)

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of the notices)

trigger: A law enforcement agency determines notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period in the agency's written request (may be extended or revoked in writing)
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the written request

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the firm (inbound)
trigger: A vendor that maintains the firm's personal information (payroll, ATS, timekeeping, screening, AI vendors) has a breach of its system
deadline: Vendor must notify the firm as expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after determination; the firm then gives notices under (3) and (4)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - register the breach contact with each vendor

trigger: Affected associates or candidates who live outside Florida (for example, former associates who moved)
notify: Residents and regulators per each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Check the residence state of every affected person from payroll and ATS addresses

citation: E-Verify MOU for Employers Art. II.A.16
trigger: Suspected or confirmed loss of control of, or unauthorized access to, E-Verify personal data (case data and results kept in the ATS I-9 module or E-Verify credentials)
notify: DHS E-Verify by phone (888-464-4218) or email (E-Verify@dhs.gov) with the subject 'Privacy Incident - Password'
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the ATS I-9 module or an E-Verify account is involved; not triggered by the payroll platform alone

obligation: IRS notice of Form W-2 data loss (guidance)
citation: IRS guidance: Form W-2/SSN data theft information for businesses and payroll service providers
trigger: Theft of employee W-2 or SSN data
deadline: As soon as possible (the IRS may be able to protect employees from tax-related identity theft if told quickly)
notify: IRS at dataloss@irs.gov with the subject 'W2 Data Loss' and a contact; do not attach employee personal information
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary but recommended; the associate register includes SSNs and pay data

trigger: Security incident affecting client information (for example, client contacts or timesheets in the ATS)
deadline: Per contract (the two largest warehouse clients require 72 hours)
notify: Client security contacts listed in the contract register
applies_at_this_tier: Only if client data is involved; associate-only data does not trigger most contracts

trigger: Suspected security incident or fraudulent funds transfer
deadline: Per policy (use the carrier's breach hotline before hiring vendors)
As soon as possible (supports recovery of diverted funds and any 501.171(4)(b) delay request)
notify: FBI IC3 online report; local FBI field office

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: An extortion demand is received and payment is considered
deadline: Before any payment; reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor

trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI held for a covered entity
deadline: No later than 60 calendar days after discovery
applies_at_this_tier: No - the firm is not a business associate (P03 G-146)

obligation: CIRCIA incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours; 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; as proposed, the firm is under its SBA size standard and meets no sector criterion

deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the firm holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
